title: Exact functors preserve bounded below derived objects
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact functor between abelian categories, and let $F:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ also denote the functor between the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induced by applying $F$ termwise to cochain complexes [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $H^r(FK)\cong F(H^rK)$, natural in $K$; when $K=Q(X)$ for a complex $X$, it is the composite $H^r(F(QX))\cong H^r(Q(FX))\cong H^r(FX)\cong F(H^rX)\cong F(H^r(QX))$ of the isomorphism $F\circ Q\cong Q\circ F$, the isomorphisms $H^r\circ Q\cong H^r$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$, and the isomorphism of complexes $H^r(FX)\cong F(H^rX)$ induced by $\ker F(d^r)=F(\ker d^r)$, $\operatorname{im}F(d^{r-1})=F(\operatorname{im}d^{r-1})$ (so the isomorphism is computed termwise on any representing complex). Consequently, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, $F$ carries $D(\mathcal A)^{\ge n}$ (the $K$ with $H^r(K)=0$ for $r<n$) into $D(\mathcal B)^{\ge n}$, hence carries the bounded below derived category $D^+(\mathcal A)$ into $D^+(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] (and likewise $D^-$ and $D^b$).

source.place: Lemma 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor): an exact functor carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and every complex computes RF, so RF is defined on D^+ and D; the preservation of the bounded (above, below) subcategories is stated in sites-cohomology.tex, Section 0735 (section-base-change-map), paragraph before Lemma 0736

proof.text: Complex level. Let $C(\mathcal A)$ denote the category of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ and $F_C:C(\mathcal A)\to C(\mathcal B)$ termwise application of $F$. For every $r$ there is an isomorphism of functors $c^r:H^r\circ F_C\xrightarrow{\sim}F\circ H^r:C(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal B$, with $c^r_X:H^r(FX)\to F(H^rX)$ induced by $\ker F(d^r)=F(\ker d^r)$ and $\operatorname{im}F(d^{r-1})=F(\operatorname{im}d^{r-1})$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. In particular $F_C$ carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms: if $H^r(s)$ is an isomorphism for all $r$, so is $H^r(F_Cs)=(c^r_Y)^{-1}\circ F(H^r(s))\circ c^r_X$ (naturality of $c^r$), which is what makes $F:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ defined [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

source.place: Lemma 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof: 'F transforms acyclic complexes into acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms'; homology.tex Lemma 010N for the degreewise homology

proof.text: The two functors on $D(\mathcal A)$ agree after composing with $Q$. Let $Q_{\mathcal A}:C(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$, $Q_{\mathcal B}$ be the localization functors and $H^r:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$, $H^r:D(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal B$ the cohomology functors, with isomorphisms $\eta_{\mathcal A}:H^r\circ Q_{\mathcal A}\cong H^r$, $\eta_{\mathcal B}:H^r\circ Q_{\mathcal B}\cong H^r$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F_D:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be the induced functor with its isomorphism $\beta:F_D\circ Q_{\mathcal A}\cong Q_{\mathcal B}\circ F_C$ [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Put $G_1=H^r\circ F_D$ and $G_2=F\circ H^r$, both functors $D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal B$. Define the natural isomorphism $\tau:G_1\circ Q_{\mathcal A}\to G_2\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$ as the composite $H^r F_DQ_{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{H^r\beta}H^rQ_{\mathcal B}F_C\xrightarrow{\eta_{\mathcal B}F_C}H^rF_C\xrightarrow{c^r}FH^r\xrightarrow{F\eta_{\mathcal A}^{-1}}FH^rQ_{\mathcal A}$ (Step 1); each factor is a natural isomorphism of functors $C(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal B$ (whiskering and composition of natural isomorphisms). Both $G_i\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$ send quasi-isomorphisms to isomorphisms, since $Q_{\mathcal A}$ does.

source.place: Lemma 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), (3)-(4): F(K^\bullet) -> RF(K^\bullet) is an isomorphism for all complexes; Section 13.11 (cohomology functors factor through Q)

proof.text: Descent to $D(\mathcal A)$. Apply the universal property of the localization $Q_{\mathcal A}$ at the quasi-isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) with $\mathcal E=\mathcal B$, $F_i:=G_i\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$, $F_i':=G_i$ and $\phi_i$ the identities: the natural transformation $\tau$ of Step 2 lifts to a unique natural transformation $c^r_D:G_1\to G_2$ with $(c^r_D)_{Q_{\mathcal A}X}=\tau_X$ for every complex $X$, and since lifting respects composition and identities, the lift of $\tau^{-1}$ is inverse to $c^r_D$. Thus $c^r_D:H^r(F_DK)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H^rK)$ is an isomorphism natural in $K\in D(\mathcal A)$, and on $K=Q_{\mathcal A}X$ it is the composite $\tau_X$ described in the statement. (Every object of $D(\mathcal A)$ is isomorphic to some $Q_{\mathcal A}X$, so by naturality $c^r_D$ is determined by these values.)

source.place: Lemma 05R7 (lemma-universal-property-localization); Stacks omits the details in Lemma 015F

proof.text: Bounded subcategories. $F$ is additive (an exact functor between abelian categories preserves finite biproducts), so $F(0)\cong0$. Let $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(\mathcal A)^{\ge n}$, i.e. $H^r(K)=0$ for $r<n$. Then for $r<n$, $H^r(F_DK)\cong F(H^rK)=F(0)\cong0$ by Step 3, so $F_DK\in D(\mathcal B)^{\ge n}$; in the same way $H^r(K)=0$ for $r>n$ gives $H^r(F_DK)=0$ for $r>n$, so $F_D$ carries $D(\mathcal A)^{\le n}$ into $D(\mathcal B)^{\le n}$. Since $D^+=\bigcup_nD^{\ge n}$, $D^-=\bigcup_nD^{\le n}$ and $D^b=D^+\cap D^-$, described by the vanishing of cohomology [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], $F_D$ carries $D^+(\mathcal A)$, $D^-(\mathcal A)$, $D^b(\mathcal A)$ into $D^+(\mathcal B)$, $D^-(\mathcal B)$, $D^b(\mathcal B)$ respectively.
